answer: A long-horizon service orchard resists Sybils: a new identity must tend one public service, such as a fresh data feed, for a full horizon before earning full spending rights. Rewards vest only if random spot checks confirm continuous uptime, and abandoning the orchard forfeits its planted bond. A comet task that appears without warning cannot be faked retroactively, so each fake identity needs its own live operator, monitoring, and uptime. Farming a thousand Sybils then costs a thousand ongoing shifts, not one cheap script.
